original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Uniform exact paid-call minimum for the 12 F2[Q8] diagonal triples with one central [-1] target and two {i,j} targets, over every finite register count r >= 3 and arbitrary dirty identity-target roles.
scope_change_reason: Q8 PR #1925 gives finite r=3,4 coverage for these 12 central-minus-one tuples but leaves arbitrary extra dirty roles open. The new result derives a uniform augmentation-ideal obstruction rather than extending the finite search or changing only its radius.
bottleneck_link: The four-call word is a formal bit-mechanism upper bound; no physical supplier mapping or selected kappa gain is asserted. The uniform obstruction closes a structural relaxation for this target family.
stop_rule: Prove the all-finite-r lower bound using J/J^2 and the exact central coefficient, check all 12 direct words and bounded idempotent controls at r=3,4, and stop; any exact three-call counterexample falsifies the claim.
evidence: README.md gives the uniform proof. CERTIFICATE.json records exact F2[Q8] algebra identities, J/J^2 dimensions, r=3,4 idempotent-pair exhaustions and direct positive/negative controls; verify.py reproduces it.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical derivation, exact finite controls, verification and writing; no independent human review is claimed.
